questions.question: In Google Ads, what determines your Ad Rank?
questions.explanation: Ad Rank = Bid × Quality Score (plus ad extensions impact). A higher Quality Score lets you pay less and still rank above competitors.

questions.question: Which three factors make up Google Ads Quality Score?
options: Expected CTR, ad relevance, and landing page experience
questions.explanation: Quality Score (1-10) is based on expected CTR, ad relevance to the keyword, and landing page experience. Improving these lowers your cost per click.

questions.question: What is the correct campaign structure hierarchy in Meta (Facebook/Instagram) Ads?
questions.explanation: Meta Ads follow Campaign (objective) > Ad Set (audience, budget, schedule) > Ad (creative and copy). Each level controls different settings.

questions.question: A shoe brand spends ₹50,000 on Google Ads and generates ₹2,00,000 in revenue. What is the ROAS?
questions.explanation: ROAS = Revenue ÷ Ad Spend = ₹2,00,000 ÷ ₹50,000 = 4x. This means every ₹1 spent returned ₹4 in revenue.

questions.question: What does Google Tag Manager (GTM) primarily help you do?
options: Manage and deploy tracking codes without editing website code
questions.explanation: GTM is a tag management system that lets marketers add tracking pixels (Google Ads, Meta Pixel, analytics) without asking developers to change code.

questions.question: What is the Meta Pixel used for?
options: Tracking user actions on your website for ad optimization and retargeting
questions.explanation: The Meta Pixel is a JavaScript snippet placed on your website that tracks conversions, builds retargeting audiences, and helps Meta optimize ad delivery.

questions.question: An ad gets 200 clicks from 10,000 impressions. What is the CTR?
questions.explanation: CTR = (Clicks ÷ Impressions) × 100 = (200 ÷ 10,000) × 100 = 2%. A 2% CTR is considered good for search ads.

questions.question: Which Google Ads campaign type shows product images, prices, and store name directly in search results?
questions.explanation: Google Shopping Ads pull product data from Merchant Center to show images, prices, and store names — ideal for e-commerce businesses.

questions.question: What is a Lookalike Audience in Meta Ads?
options: People who already bought from you
A new audience that resembles your existing customers based on data patterns
People who liked your Facebook page
questions.explanation: Lookalike Audiences use Meta's algorithm to find new people who share characteristics with your best existing customers, expanding your reach to similar prospects.

questions.question: You spent ₹30,000 on ads and got 150 conversions. What is your CPA?
questions.explanation: CPA (Cost Per Acquisition) = Total Spend ÷ Conversions = ₹30,000 ÷ 150 = ₹200. Lower CPA means more efficient spending.

questions.question: Which YouTube ad format can be skipped after 5 seconds?
questions.explanation: TrueView In-stream ads play before/during videos and can be skipped after 5 seconds. You only pay when viewers watch 30 seconds or interact.

questions.question: What is the maximum duration of a YouTube Bumper Ad?
questions.explanation: Bumper Ads are non-skippable and limited to 6 seconds. They are best for brand awareness with a short, memorable message.

questions.question: Which bidding strategy should you use if your goal is to get maximum conversions within a fixed budget?
questions.explanation: Maximize Conversions uses Google's AI to automatically set bids that get the most conversions within your daily budget.

questions.question: In A/B testing ads, what is the correct approach?
options: Change headline, image, CTA, and audience all at once
Change only one variable at a time to identify what works
Run both ads for 1 hour and pick the winner
Always test with the lowest possible budget
questions.explanation: A/B testing changes one variable at a time (e.g., only the headline) so you can clearly attribute performance differences to that specific change.

questions.question: A local coaching class in Pune wants to target students within 5 km. Which targeting option is most appropriate?
questions.explanation: Location/radius targeting lets you show ads only to people within a specific distance from your business — perfect for local services.

questions.question: What does CPM stand for in advertising?
questions.explanation: CPM = Cost Per Mille (1,000 impressions). If CPM is ₹100, you pay ₹100 for every 1,000 times your ad is shown, regardless of clicks.

questions.question: Which LinkedIn Ad format works best for generating B2B leads with a form that auto-fills user data?
questions.explanation: LinkedIn Lead Gen Forms pre-fill the user's profile data (name, email, company) making it easy to submit — resulting in higher conversion rates for B2B.

questions.question: What is Google Performance Max?
options: A manual campaign type for search only
An AI-driven campaign that runs across all Google channels automatically
questions.explanation: Performance Max uses Google's AI to run ads across Search, Display, YouTube, Gmail, Maps, and Discover from a single campaign, optimizing for your conversion goals.

questions.question: An e-commerce store has 1,000 website visitors but only 20 purchases. They want to bring back the other 980 visitors. Which strategy should they use?
questions.explanation: Retargeting shows ads to people who already visited your site but didn't convert. These warm audiences typically convert at 3-5x higher rates than cold audiences.

questions.question: If your Google Ads campaign has a daily budget of ₹1,000 and your average CPC is ₹10, approximately how many clicks can you expect per day?
questions.explanation: Expected clicks = Daily Budget ÷ Avg CPC = ₹1,000 ÷ ₹10 = 100 clicks. This helps you forecast traffic before launching.
